headline: Revised zoning ordinance package, a special permit at 131-133 Westfield Road, and a proposed GLOVE gloves ban.

Meeting will take place at Holyoke City Hall, 536 Dwight St
and can also be accessed remotely via www.zoom.us
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/85914960000?pwd=QVBqSkJvd0pSZENmNFdDbnVXTnVTUT09
Meeting ID: 859 1496 0000 Meeting Passcode: 657908 or by call in at 1 (646) 558-8656 with
same Meeting ID and Passcode.
Live Spanish interpretation will be available on local access channel 15 using the television's
SAP option, through the live stream on the city website, as well as on the Zoom feed by clicking
the interpretation option and choosing Spanish.
Thursday, November 5, 2026
6:30 PM
AGENDA
PRESIDENT'S REPORT
PUBLIC HEARING
PUBLIC COMMENT
REGULAR AND PENDING EXECUTIVE SESSION MINUTES
1. June 11, 2024, September 4, 2024, and April 15, 2025 Executive Session Minutes -
Reviewed and ready for partial release as of September 17, 2025
2. December 9, 2024 Finance Committee Executive Session Minutes - Reviewed and withheld
in entirety as of September 17, 2025
3. From City Clerk Brenna Murphy Leary and Admin. Assistant Jeffery Anderson-Burgos,
meeting minutes from October 20, 2026.
LAID ON THE TABLE
4. Vacon- Greaney- ORDER: that city council go to the first ballot to elect a treasurer at the
April 21, 2026 city council meeting in accordance with our current charter. Our city council
appointed Collector has indicated interest in the Treasurer/Collector position. A majority of the
city council has had the opportunity to interview our Collector. This appointment would legally
establish the Treasurer position & for practical purposes combines the positions, while waiting
for further charter changes that will be sent to the state legislature in a home rule petition.
Transition changes can happen in coordination with other ordinance changes.
COMMUNICATIONS
5. From Mayor Joshua Garcia-letter appointing Mr. Scott Geiger of 63 Cherry St. to serve on
the Planning Board. Mr. Geiger will serve a five-year term expiring June 30, 2031
6. From City Solicitor Lisa Ball-Appointments to the Board of Assessors
7. From Deborah Brunelle, Chief Assessor-letter of retirement
8. From City Comptroller Sharon Bittner Willis, FY2027 Sewer Enterprise Expense YTD
Report-Totals
9. From City Comptroller Sharon Bittner-Willis, FY2027 General Fund Expense YTD
Report-Totals
10. From Holyoke Redevelopment Authority-meeting minutes from September 16, 2026.
11. From HEDIC-meeting minutes from June 20, 2026, August 13, 2026, and HEDIC's
2025-2026 Annual Meeting Summary
12. From City of Holyoke Health Benefit Meeting-meeting minutes from September 15, 2026
13. From the Planning Board- revised zoning ordinance package
14. Planning Board NOD - Rafael & Sheila Rivera at 230-232 Beech for Increase in Fence
Height
15. Planning Board NOD - Palladium Holdings at 61-69 Suffolk for Reduction of Parking
Requirements
PETITIONS
16. Petition from EcoATM for a second hand license at 515 High St. (kiosk inside Sam's Food
Stores)
REPORTS OF COMMITTEES
17. The Committee on Charter and Rules to whom was referred an order that the City Council
(1) perform a comprehensive review of the Council Rules, in order to identify internal
inconsistencies and redundancies, ambiguous provisions, archaic language, and areas where
further information is necessary or desirable to construe said Rules; and (2) draft and adopt
such amendments to the Rules as are found to be appropriate or necessary in light of said
review. This order is intended to allow the Council's committees to examine and recommend,
and the Council to vote upon, technical corrections packages on an ongoing basis, rather than
requiring the preparation of a single, comprehensive package of corrections or multiple single
and specific orders for changes. In the event that the Law Department finds that more
specificity is needed to conform to the Open Meetings Law, the makers of the order shall work
with the Law Department to amend it to satisfy those additional requirements, and this Order
shall be deemed to be so amended.
Awaiting disposition
18. The Committee on Charter and Rules to whom was referred an order At the request of the
Law Department, ordered: that the City Council approve a home rule petition for the purpose of
obtaining an Article 97 land exchange to satisfy a ROW taking needed for the Beech St
intersection project.
Awaiting disposition
19. The Committee on Charter and Rules to whom was referred an order Add to rule 9h: when
an order has been deemed tabled after the chair has not taken it up for 45 business days, upon
request of the maker, the chair shall place the order on the next agenda to ensure compliance
with the open meeting law.
Awaiting disposition
20. The Committee on Charter and Rules to whom was referred an order that the Council
Rules be examined and revised as necessary to clarify the Rule 9 provisions relating to legal
form and committee procedure.
Awaiting disposition
21. The Committee on Charter and Rules to whom was referred an order that the City Council
amend its Rules to establish clearer and more stringent guidelines governing Public Comment,
including, but not limited to, requiring that individuals participating remotely keep their cameras
on while speaking during Public Comment.
Awaiting disposition
22. The Committee on Charter and Rules to whom was referred an order that the Council
amend its rules to allow the Council President to sit down during all Council meetings, and to
provide the President with a chair of appropriate height to see over the podium.
Awaiting disposition
MOTIONS, ORDERS AND RESOLUTIONS
23. Anderson-Burgos - Ordered that the City Council vote on appointing its representative to
the Holyoke Media Board. The seat is currently held by Daniel O'Sullivan for a 3-year term,
which expired on June 30, 2026. Mr. O'Sullivan has expressed interest in being reappointed to
a new 3-year term, expiring on June 30, 2029.
24. Devine- ORDERED: Respectfully ask the Planning Board or at least 2 members of the
Board conduct their meetings in person, especially those dealing with the development of
Wyckoff Country Club.
25. DEVINE: ORDERED that Maureen Cronin be appointed to the Board of Assessors to a
term of 11/5/26 through 12/31/26.
26. Devine- ORDERED that the Planning Board meet IN PERSON in the Planning Board
conference room or the room near the City Council chambers regarding Walmart Super Store
on the date they have chosen. This will allow the public to speak.
27. DEVINE: ORDERED that Grant Schlosstein's current appointment to the Board of
Assessors be amended to fill Anthony Dulude's term of 1/1/25-1/1/28.

34. Magrath-Smith - that the Law Dept. provide guidance to the City Council as to the new (and
proposed) state statutes governing zoning variances given the recent withdrawal of the 12
Crescent Street application.
35. Maisonet- Ordered that the DPW install a Handicap placard for Juanita McKoy at 201
Clemente St. PL#7450904
36. Panitch, Thalheimer: Ordered, that the Council be provided with lists of real properties that
are, or are likely to become, subject to the provisions of Article III, Section 2-336 of the Holyoke
Code of Ordinances, and that said lists be maintained and updated as the status of said
properties changes, by the following officers or their designees:
(1) The Treasurer or Tax Title Custodian: Property acquired by the city through the foreclosure
of tax titles or pursuant to M.G.L.A. c. 60, §§ 79-80B;
(2) The City Solicitor: Real property in tax title litigation, along with the status of said litigation;
(3) The City Solicitor: Real property acquired by the city by any other means, along with
properties in any stage of the process of acquisition by the city, and the status thereof.
37. Panitch, Thalheimer: Ordered, pursuant to Section 48 of the Charter, that the Problem
Properties Group provide written reports to the City Council within 30 business days of each
meeting, which shall at minimum provide (a) a list of properties under review by the PPG,
whether discussed in said meeting or not; (b) a comprehensive summary of the properties
discussed, their status as of the meeting, strategies considered, and decisions made with
respect to each of said properties; and (c) a summary of any discussions of potential policies
considered to address the issues that the PPG encounters in its work.
38. Thalheimer, Panitch: Ordered, that per discussion in the Public Safety committee, the City
of Holyoke ban the use of GLOVE (Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter) gloves within the
City by any agency, person, or authority; and further Ordered that no funds available to the City
be expended to acquire GLOVEs for or by any agency or department of the City or under the
City's control, including without limitation taxpayer revenues, grants, or gifts; and further
Ordered that no gift of such gloves may be accepted by the City from any source, including but
not limited to state, regional, or federal law enforcement sources. Send to Ordinance.
39. Thalheimer - Invite the Tree Warden and Director of Conservation to attend an upcoming
Public Safety meeting to present a plan for addressing vacant tree pits, stumps, hazardous
trees, and other outstanding tree related needs throughout the City. Send to Public Safety.

Rivera, I. - Order that the portion of Cabot Street from South Bridge Street to South Summer
Street be named "Capri Way" in honor of Capri Pizza and its longstanding presence in the
Holyoke community.
Per City Council rule 2B, meeting shall end by 10 PM unless an extension is approved by a
two-thirds majority of those present. If any items remain, those items will be added to the
beginning of the next regular meeting.
The listing of matters are those reasonably anticipated by the chair which may be
discussed at the meeting.
